requirements.quote: QUIC starts a loss epoch when a packet is lost.
requirements.condition: A QUIC packet is declared lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Start a loss epoch when the packet is lost.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave the connection outside a loss epoch after declaring the packet lost.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-processing trace can verify that declaring a packet lost transitions the congestion controller into a loss epoch.

requirements.quote:
The loss epoch ends
   when any packet sent after the start of the epoch is acknowledged.
requirements.condition: While a loss epoch is active, any packet sent after that epoch began is acknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: End the active loss epoch upon that acknowledgment.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not keep that loss epoch active after acknowledging a packet sent after its start.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can record the epoch start, packet send times, and acknowledgment processing, then assert that the qualifying acknowledgment terminates the epoch.

requirements.quote:
both should reduce their
   congestion windows only once per epoch
requirements.condition: QUIC processes losses belonging to one loss epoch.
requirements.required_behavior: Reduce the congestion window once for that loss epoch.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reduce the congestion window more than once within the same loss epoch.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject multiple losses before the epoch-ending acknowledgment and count congestion-window reductions for the epoch.

requirements.quote:
QUIC will do it once for
   every round trip that experiences loss
requirements.condition: A QUIC round trip experiences packet loss.
requirements.required_behavior: Perform one congestion-window reduction for that loss-experiencing round trip.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the congestion-window reduction for a round trip that experiences loss or perform it more than once for that round trip.
requirements.why_checkable: A multi-round-trip loss trace can associate loss events and congestion-window changes with each round trip and verify exactly one reduction per affected round trip.
